entries.body: Mixed feelings about South Africa. We spent 3 days at the Tuzi Gazi marina in Richards Bay — Shadowfax was there, also Heart's Content and ABV, Sterling & Stella Maris followed us in. We organized a trip to the Hluhluwe Game Park with Stella Maris & Sterling — had a fantastic time! We saw wildebeests, buffalo, warthogs, rhinos, zebras, giraffes, impalas, baboons, monkeys, nyalas, kudus, and one elephant. Encountered a 'rhino road block' at one point and had to turn around. The landscape was very stark — rolling hills & plains with few large trees. It is extremely dry and the animals were searching for water. We had a wonderful day, hanging out of the van taking pictures. We drove through some spread-out Zulu villages and saw their typical architecture — one round grass thatched building for sleeping, 2 other small square buildings for storage, etc. The children were spread out for miles along the roads, walking to school. White people are all very scared and we can't walk anywhere — everything in cars. What a hassle. We moved to a mooring at the Zululand Yacht Club & passed 5 peaceful days there — I could even get swim! But we have southeast winds today so we are out of here. Bedouin, Just Jinx, & Golden Sovereign arrived from the Mozambique channel and already headed on. Sterling and a South African boat, Kiren, are sailing with us. Also got to see Pierre on Quo Vadis again. Brian spent a couple of evenings with Shawn, that was good.

Very uncomfortable night, waves from every direction but the wind held and we approached Durban after sunrise. Huge skyline. I think this is the biggest city we have ever sailed to. Harbor is nasty but the city has everything we need, including a new boom! Dos Tintos is here.

Maybe this time we will succeed in leaving Durban! We left Tuesday but turned around after 24 hours when the wind turned SW. But we did accomplish something after our return — got the new UV cover sewn on the furler with the invaluable help of Dos Tintos' sewing machine! Had ours tuned & parts replaced as well. Finally met the Japanese family on Akitsushima and had Pierre on Quo Vadis & Dietmar on Anke 2 over for dinner. This time we waited until the wind had definitely turned east before we left. A bit of motoring, but we finally caught the Agulhas current before sundown. Thanks to Tintos who told us where it was! We are happy to be out of Durban with the nasty water. We did go to the beach and craft market one day — bought Zulu baskets, walking sticks and a massive carved rhino to remind us of our experience in Hluhluwe game park. Met Fred the net guy and his wife Eva and had lunch at their house. Replaced the broken boom, fixed some other stuff. So it was a useful stop but the city was big, scary and dirty. Could only walk within a 5-block radius of the marina. People sleeping in the streets.

Today is Lynne's 50th birthday — she did not want to be reminded of it! Don't blame her, being over 50 is no fun. Had a great ride last night — speeds up to 11.7 and averaged 10 knots for hours. Winds picked up a bit for a while but always from the east. Hard to keep in the current, especially farther south where it is narrower. We are doing almost 10 now, with 10 knots from the east and flat seas — quite nice! Should be in East London sometime after dark, hope Tintos will be around to help us. 240 miles in less than 36 hours! What a ride. Saw whales jumping yesterday when we left, none today.

Too short a time in East London — the wind turned favorable today and we had to move on. Brian was quite disappointed as he was having a good time hanging out with Shawn from Golden Sovereign. a braai was planned for tonight at their house, we hated to miss it, but we know you have to go when the wind blows. Saw Chris from Bedouin briefly, took a walk to the beach — beautiful sand dunes. The highlight was meeting Anna again after 20 years! We had met her, her 2 sets of twins, & Scottish husband in Las Olas anchorage, Ft. Lauderdale, when we were on Wanderly. She had wanted to take Salty but couldn't for some reason. She invited me to do yoga with her the other morning. She is now alone on a steel boat she built herself. We really enjoyed seeing her again. So now we have 10 knots SE, light seas, beam reaching between the N & S-bound shipping lanes. It will be a sleepless night.
Sunshine, sailing downwind in flat water, sand dunes on the beach. Gwendolyn & Dos Tintos are already in Port Elizabeth. It was a quiet night. Will be tied up to the wall this afternoon.

Port Elizabeth was a real dump. Had to motorsail the last 20 miles and we hated it when we arrived. Did find a dock space that Craig on Gwendolyn had arranged. He & Tintos spent all their time in the yacht club bar of course. Got rained in for 2 days, absolutely nothing to do but walk to the grocery store and have a cheap ice cream. We left early this morning, hoping for a good southerly breeze. We are now sailing west, just south of 34° S. The wind is painfully light, motored for 7 hours, now barely moving. How we love South Africa! It did improve! Sailing at 3–4 knots, not so bad. Coastline is getting more interesting.

It was a pleasant night, after the wind turned just north of east and we jibed. The sky was beautiful last night and we were close enough to see the mountains. Rugged coastline here, narrow rocky plain with mountains rising behind. It was slow yesterday, but we made up for it early in the morning when we were surfing over 8 knots. So we will make Mossel Bay before dark. Tintos is rounding Cape Agulhas this afternoon. We hope to have some fun here!

On the road again, after a rather pleasant, if somewhat lonely, interlude at Mossel Bay. Tied to a mooring outside the harbor, wasn't too bad in a westerly wind. The yacht club was not particularly friendly. We enjoyed walking around the town, along the cliffs, swimming and walking on the beach. Saw a replica of Bartholomew Diaz' caravel at the museum, he landed in Mossel Bay in 1488. The town was mostly white, clean, full of tourists. Left at 5 this morning, motored 9 hours before the SE wind came up, what an agony. Cape Agulhas by sunrise tomorrow.

Great sailing around the cape! Last night was calm, 4–5 knots downwind with clear skies, lots of stars, the Southern Cross in the sky. We passed Cape Agulhas at sunrise. We had seals all around the boat, checking us out. Then the wind picked up and we have been flying NW towards Cape Point. One cape after another appears in front of us. We will be back in the Atlantic soon. After a rough start, this has turned into a fine sail. Will be in Capetown sometime tonight. Yeah!

On the road again — first New Years at sea. Left Capetown, finally, yesterday. Got stuck waiting for Brian's Christmas present to arrive. Spent Christmas at the yacht club, Steve & Julie on Dos Tintos organized a barbeque. It lasted well into the night, full moon, some people got really drunk. We enjoyed meeting Alana & Dany on Thai and did some hiking with them up Lions Peak and Table Mountain. That almost killed us, even Brian was tired and happy to take the cable car back down. Great view up there, fun to get away from the harbor and out in the green. Also met Steve the Kiwi on Long White Cloud. Stella Maris & Quo Vadis showed up. But we decided to forego the New Years Eve party and get going across the Atlantic instead. Yesterday was very slow, mostly becalmed for 12 hours in front of Table Mountain. Wind picked up steadily at night and by 8 am we were reefing. Wind from SW and big westerly swell keeps throwing us around. No celebration tonight — too rough! But Brian is content to play his new Game Boy games so it doesn't matter. We are very happy to be done with Africa!

Happy New Year! It was a boisterous one — must have been blowing at least 30 when the new year rolled around. Had to take the main down until morning. Still blowing S 25, we are poled out, averaging 7 knots. A bit more comfortable than last night but still cold! Showers are no fun. Started school today — oh joy. Everyone in a good mood, glad to be away from Africa.

Another wild ride last night with the main down. Talked to Eddie on F-Mmm, he had the same 25–35 knots. Today it is down to 10; swells are down, comfortable but slower. Nothing out here but us. Forgot to mention the penguin that swam after us on Thursday, when we were going slow, 20 miles from shore. Was he looking for a resting place? He emitted some mournful honks, I think he was lost.

I used to write smaller & more clearly, looking back on my old logs. I will try to do better! We have 4 sails up today, 15 knots of wind, gorgeous sailing. The weather is getting warmer every day, but it is still not hot. We hope to keep the wind with us — it's fun to go fast! m.

Wind started dying last night at sunset, so we slowed down considerably. Tried to sail so far east, we knew it would happen. Now we are sailing north, trying to pick the wind back up. It is quite pleasant however, hot & sunny, we're soaking it up on deck! Water is a beautiful blue.

Another light day but we are moving at a steady 4.5 knots. Back on the right track after heading north all yesterday to find more wind. Air is warmer, the shower water was actually hot. The ocean is still blue and empty.. Better tomorrow!
Woke up with breakfast on the deck — a 12" squid! Thomas fried it up and enjoyed it. Wind still light, we have the mizzen drifter up now, but it doesn't do much. Life is peaceful.
Caught a dorado late yesterday afternoon — so we are officially in the tropics now! Wind picked up some, turned SSE.
Windy today and we are charging along at a steady 6 knots. Sometimes the clouds completely cover the sky and then they disappear altogether. Ocean crossing is a pretty weird business.

Woke up to 100% overcast this morning, cool air. We passed 20° S, and 0° E this afternoon — we are now officially back in the western hemisphere. We sailed into yesterday after 2½ years in tomorrow. The sun peeks out occasionally but it is not tropical. Moving along at a good speed, had to jibe so we are now on the uncomfortable tack — Brian and I keep flying around the cabin.

Hoping for sun today but no go. Can tell that it would be hot if it was out. Sky cleared up completely last night — starry sky. Today we just got some rain, not enough to wash though. Less than 300 miles to go. Still have seen nothing out here.

We spent an hour on deck this afternoon, enjoying the sun before the clouds moved back in. It has been another gray day, winds are light. We won't make St. Helena until the end of the day tomorrow. Hope for some more sunshine.

Island landfalls are so much more satisfying than continents! We love islands. St. Helena appeared in the haze, under a topping of clouds, around 30 miles out. It looks huge, with some high peaks. We are tuned into the local AM radio station, they play music from another era and are concerned about a water shortage. We will be anchored by sunset. Clear skies today, 10–15 K SE tradewind — why couldn't we have this yesterday? Looking forward to a short rest — 1700 miles behind us!

What a perfect day to leave on a journey! We enjoyed St. Helena so much, we decided to stay the weekend. We took a tour of the island and saw its lush interior with green valleys. Learned more than we cared to know about Napoleon's exile, and had lunch on his tomb. I had a long swim in the big pool. The outside of the island was rocky & barren, but the interior is a hidden gem. The people were very friendly — we were the only visitors on the island as there is no airport. Our arrival was announced on the local radio station. The water was crystal clear, deep blue, we could see the bottom 50 feet down. Only drawback was the rolly anchorage. Today we are suffering from sore leg muscles, after climbing the 700 steps in Jacob's Ladder, a stairway to the top of the cliff on one side of the little city, Jamestown, which was in the crack of a valley. It was very quaint with European-style houses squeezed together. Next stop Fernando de Noronha, another 1730 miles.

stops.name: St. Helena to Fernando de Noronha

entries.body: So much for perfect trade wind sailing. Wind got light last night, even lighter today. Managing to maintain 4 knots until now. Cirrus clouds down south. Oh well — lots of sunshine anyway! Catching up on our rest, rolling less than St. Helena anchorage!

We sure hate the idea of going back to cars and crowds and hustling. Hard to imagine overpopulation in the South Atlantic Ocean — it is so empty here. Nothing to write — the days pass pleasantly, lots of sunshine, enough wind to do100+ miles a day. Got out the sextant & gave Brian a lesson on noon sights.

Big excitement yesterday morning — the Moorings catamaran we met in St. Helena motored up to us and took pictures! Very light wind, motored for a couple of hours. Had a good night of sailing but now it's dropping again. This will set a record for the slowest passage!

Incredible to be ghosting along at 3.5–4 knots in this flat calm sea! How expectations can change — we are content to do 100 miles a day. I think this is the most enjoyable ocean voyage we have ever had — everyone is content with the moment, the 3 of us out here in the gentle sea. I am reading Desperate Voyage — his trip was totally different from ours. I would like to have kittens aboard too. Been running off the wind with poled-out genoa, main & mizzen, mizzen drifter up forward, but now we are reaching as the wind has turned NE. Can't seem to make any northing. On our uncomfortable tack, but it makes no difference in these benign conditions.

We have a shark swimming along next to the boat for hours now. First time we have ever seen this, although we have heard of it. At least it looks like a shark — it's not a dolphin. Got some wind today, not steady, but we are doing 5 at times. Then it drops away and we wallow. Brian enjoys taking noon sights, although he hates the math. Life proceeds at a calm pace out here.

Time passes — we keep hoping the wind will pick up & stay up, but it never does. Had a colorful full moonrise 2 nights ago. It was blood red. Last night Brian thought the moon was a fluorescent orange life raft! It isn't a shark swimming with us — it's a 4-foot yellow fin tuna! He likes to show off for us, jumping after flying fish. Thomas wants to eat him of course. Also have 2 small stripey fish who have been with us a long time. Lots of sunshine, lots of rolling, but we move on.

What a great night — no banging of sails, slamming of main boom. Wind held up all night, did 5 knots. Today down to 4 again but it's better than 3! Getting hotter every day. Lost our yellowfin after Thomas made a harpoon. But we now have 3 stripey fish with us.

Finally moving again! Wind has picked up steadily, took the drifter down this morning, doing 6 knots with 3 sails now. The end is in sight! Also connected to a Winlink station in Trinidad last evening, so everyone is happy. Enjoy watching the miles count down, although it is not so comfortable as during the calm. It was another perfect night with lots of stars, waning moon, balmy breeze.

After all those days of slow sailing with no wind, now we are flying in 20 knots and we have to slow down! Wind came up yesterday and we began flying in the evening. Now we have to reef more to slow down — doing 7 knots. We don't want to arrive in Fernando de Noronha before sunrise tomorrow. Seas are big and we are rolling. Guess the calm wasn't so bad! It is fun to see the miles roll down though. It has been a good passage altogether. Had a bird on the dinghy motor all night — he moved to the solar cell this morning and finally flew away. Just saw a big ship pass by close. Looking forward to a swim.

Had a perfect sunrise landfall at Fernando. Were surprised to see 3 boats there — they had arrived from Cape Verde. It was extremely hot on shore and no one spoke English. But we loved the Brazilian flavor — the melodious language, the good-looking people in all colors, everyone friendly. Thomas downed lots of cold beers. We took the bus around the island, it is volcanic & very dry. Played in the waves on the most perfect surf beach we have ever seen. Enjoyed the clear blue water, the show the spinner dolphins put on every morning, jumping and spinning in the air, the cleanliness. Guess since it's a tourist island, it is kept spotless. Brian finally got to see real-life Brazilian bikinis, and he liked what he saw! We had a great time. Left this morning, 10 knots of wind north of east, forward of the beam but flat seas. 1900 miles to Tobago. What a fun stop — we like Brazil!

Light winds — 10 knots east — but since we are reaching, we are making decent 5.5 knots. Easy sailing again — the way we like it. Discovered last night that the mast head LED light is not working — too bad, no way to fix it now. School is on again, we appreciated the 4 days vacation. More blue stuff and white stuff, nothing else.

Crossed the equator at 12:20 GMT today, after almost exactly 3 years in the Southern hemisphere. Had a nice squall with rain to push us over at 7 knots. It didn't last of course! We toasted Neptune with a glass of cachaça — he should like that! Passed a long liner last night, nothing else is up.

Rain, rain go away. We are right in the middle of the ITCZ and it has been raining since last night, almost nonstop. Wind died for a while before sunrise so we motored a few hours. Been collecting water, taking lots of showers! Moving well, 5 knots average. Hope to be out of it tomorrow.. Caught a big wahoo this morning!

What a nasty day & night! But we may be through the worst now. It rained all night, the wind turned & died, we motored for a while. Rain seems to be over, wind is up & down. We are north of the ITCZ, should get steady wind soon. Tired of the constant changes!

Picked up a brisk NE trade last afternoon, made 7 knots all night long. Skies cleared up today, wind still blowing and we are trucking! We like seeing the miles fly by. Must have some current with us, supposed to be a knot or so along here. Air was very hot & humid last night — I have never sweated so much on a passage. Brian is busying himself with writing projects, he is quite resourceful, only occasionally bored. [miles]

Wind picked up last night — 20–25 NNE — had to put a 2nd reef in the main — it has been a long time. Just got nailed by a huge breaker that tore the grommets out of the weather cloth. Ride is somewhat uncomfortable, wind on the beam. We have been spoiled by the South Atlantic! Heat is hard to take, sweating all the time with hatches closed. Otherwise nice weather, welcome back to the NE trades! Sky at night has changed considerably. Big Dipper is prominent again, Orion is no longer at the zenith. Will miss the Southern Cross.

No one on Charlotte cares that it is Valentine's Day. Had lots of squally weather with gusts up to 30 knots. Going fast though. Now wind appears to be easing, veering more to the east — it will make life easier. We love the speeds. Looks like we have a total distance to Tobago of 2000 miles and we will be halfway there sometime this evening. Still sweating a lot but the water is cooler.

Sailed into some really confused seas last evening, then got nailed by a huge squall before midnight. After that, something happened — a strong counter current we suppose. Speed down to 4 knots, seas big, wind still blowing. Very uncomfortable motion, breakers washing over boat. Love the North Atlantic! Wind letting off now, squalls are gone, hazy sunshine. Speed pitiful, course off.

Put out the Walker log today and verified that we have a 1.5 knot counter current for almost 48 hours now. Pretty frustrating! Heading more west hoping to get out of it. No mention in any of the books or charts. We would be doing a steady 6 knots otherwise. Squalls are finally gone, wind down to 15, under full sail again.

Getting annoyed by this current! Losing 30 miles a day that we are sailing to nowhere. More squalls last night, Thomas got bashed by a breaker when he was reefing. Weather is oppressive today — overcast, wind 10–15, very humid. Tempers a bit short!

Finally left the current behind yesterday, now we have ¾ knot with us. The seas have flattened, sailing is perfect. Last night was beautiful with a half moon, the Dipper & the Southern Cross shining like beacons. Going to windward now but with good speed. Yesterday went downwind for a while and that sure was pleasant — could do things on deck. Still sweating buckets.

The squalls didn't stay away for long! Had plenty last night, then they quit and let us have some rest. Another big one this morning that stirred the seas up so we are rocking & rolling. Current up to 1 knot in our favor. Lots of sunshine.

Nasty rough squally night — one squall with gusts to 35 knots — we were feeling pretty weary by 3 am. Let off some then and started clearing after sunrise. Wind down now, we have let one reef out, sun is shining but the seas are still big. Best thing is that with the current and the wind, we are charging along and will be in Charlotteville, Tobago, by sunset tomorrow! Just saw a 30–40 ft. local boat, heading on a reciprocal course to nowhere we guess.
Last day at sea! We are 20 miles from Tobago and still can't see anything. It was another windy night, lots of reefing — then no wind between squalls. Ready to celebrate 5400 miles of ocean sailing!
